correctness.rationale: Connected semi-balanced graphs admit a layer functional ℓ(h)−ℓ(t)=1 and affine hull with coordinate sum zero and ℓ pairing one (dimension |V|−2). Projection of zero into this affine hull is c=ℓ0/s, s=||ℓ0||²; for every edge root v=e_h−e_t, ||v||²=2, ⟨v,c⟩=||c||²=1/s, giving radius² 2−1/s. A common vertex sphere is minimum enclosing iff c lies in the convex hull: convex averaging gives a sharp lower bound and strict separation gives a smaller shifted sphere otherwise. Edge convex combinations yield nonnegative unit flows. For A→B, c=(-1/p,1/q), radius²=2−1/p−1/q; flow marginals 1/p and 1/q are feasible iff proportional Hall p|N(X)|≥q|X| by max-flow/min-cut. Biregularity supplies uniform edge weights. These are valid under standard Euclidean realization and |V|≥3.

originality.rationale: FAIL by decisive published stronger-result implication. The complete prior Resultary theorem on rank-variance spheres of connected graded quivers proves the same all-vertex sphere, minimum-enclosing iff the center is a nonnegative unit edge flow, AND a stronger lower-ideal cut criterion for ALL graded quivers. Semi-balanced directed graphs with ℓ(h)−ℓ(t)=1 are exactly such graded quivers, up to reversing the sign convention on each root vector. The submitted bipartite proportional Hall inequalities are the two-rank specialization of that general flow/cut theorem. No independent original remainder survives.
residual_risks: No originality uncertainty material to the decision: the complete stronger theorem was materially read, and explicit sign-convention equivalence was proved.
